summary: Research every learn category for deep-dive sub-lesson candidates

subs.title: the spec marker
subs.dek: How a workbook identifies and describes itself from the inside — the inline org spec and embedded source markers that make the format filename-independent and self-explaining.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/workbook.ex (format identified by <script id="workbook-spec"> and <script id="workbook-org">, never the filename); web/learn/hello-workbook.html (a live workbook that narrates its own anatomy); web/learn/workbook.html itself carries a workbook-spec block at the bottom of its source

subs.title: tangling
subs.dek: The literate-programming move at the heart of the format: one org source tangles into the finished HTML artifact, and the source rides inside it so any recipient can unbundle and re-author.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs (render, tangle_plan, validate, parse_headlines — the OQL kernel the CLI embeds); cli/src/local.rs bundle() (oql::render + lint gate refusing dirty sources, workbook.org packed alongside workbook.html with the comment 'source travels with the artifact')

subs.title: bundling and unbundling
subs.dek: What a .wbundle actually is — a plain zip of workbook.html + workbook.org + vfs.sqlite + manifest.json — and the exact round trip: bundle, ship, unbundle, restore, with nothing proprietary in the container.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/bundle.ex (pack/ship/restore/verify, format "wbundle/1", 'because it's a plain zip, any tool can open it'); cli/src/local.rs bundle()/unbundle()/unzip_bytes_to() (byte-compatible local lane, zip-slip guard); cli/src/main.rs Cmd::Bundle/Cmd::Unbundle verbs

subs.title: nesting
subs.dek: Workbooks inside workbooks: the org tree makes every workbook a graftable subtree, nested workflows compile into one DAG of sub-worlds with typed imports/exports, and an upgrade gate keeps combining and removing safe.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs build_world() (recursive sub-worlds, 'the whole tree compiles into one nested DAG'), subtree_end() (the combine/remove unit), sig_of() per-world imports/exports, check_upgrade() (Motoko-style compatibility gate); runtime/host/exec_broker.ex @max_depth (bounded nesting, host-brokered flat forest)

subs.title: what ships and what stays
subs.dek: The privacy default behind every share: bundling exposes the work, never the session that produced it — agent memory, scratch, and telemetry stay home unless the owner explicitly opts in.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/private.ex (one source of truth: private globs/dirs, public_volumes — only 'workspace' ships; memory and tmp stay); runtime/host/bundle.ex ship() (Workbooks.VFS.public_only applied unless include_private: true, private_included recorded in the manifest); runtime/host/vfs.ex public_only/1

subs.title: sealed sections
subs.dek: How a public file carries genuinely private parts: AES-256-GCM envelopes whose keys never ship in the bundle, escrowed at the runtime and released only after a posture check — a real gate, not a login screen drawn over readable bytes.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/bundle/sealed.ex (the wbseal1 envelope: magic + iv + tag + ciphertext, AAD-bound paths, fail-closed open); runtime/host/bundle/escrow.ex and key_wrap.ex (key escrow + per-entry keys); runtime/host/bundle.ex seal_gated/key_refs manifest flow and open/2 via a KeyProvider; teased in web/learn/workbook.html FAQ

subs.title: signing and verifying
subs.dek: Make provenance travel with the bytes: sign a workbook with a self-certifying did:key (Ed25519 over canonical JSON, embedded in the file) and verify both the signature and that the artifact hasn't been touched since.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/manifest.ex (embedded <script type="application/workbooks-c2pa+json"> manifest, two-check verify: signature + asset sha256, canonical-JSON contract); cli/src/local.rs sign/verify ('byte-compatible with Workbooks.Manifest'); runtime/host/bundle.ex ship() signing on egress; the wbx sign/verify story in web/learn/workbook.html's terminal block

subs.title: the dock
subs.dek: The reader understands the Dock as a typed capability membrane: the host hands a workbook only the functions its grants permit, so a component asking for an ungranted power fails to even instantiate.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/instance/imports.ex (the `workbooks:engine` imports map, gating 'by construction'); runtime/host/rust_dock.ex and js_dock.ex (the same membrane for compiled Rust/JS core modules); runtime/host/secret_broker.ex (sign-but-never-read secrets — the host holds the key, the guest only ever sees the signature); brokers for exec/queue/tcp/udp/tls (exec_broker.ex, queue_broker.ex, tcp_broker.ex). Parent page says 'grants, not inheritance' in one sentence — this page is the mechanism.

subs.title: what a workbook may do
subs.dek: The reader can read and reason about a Policy profile: the four standard profiles, how each maps to a memory ceiling, a wall-clock CPU trap, and a capability list — and why a minimal profile literally has no network stack.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/policy.ex — the @profiles table (minimal/network/posix/compute with memory caps 64–256MB, cap lists, 5–60s timeouts), store_limits/1 (a component growing past its cap traps), timeout/1 (runaway calls trapped at the boundary, BEAM stays responsive), allow_http?/1 (the single switch that removes wasi:http, socket inheritance, AND DNS for non-net profiles — security finding wb-sec #7 documented in-module).

subs.title: the life of an instance
subs.dek: The reader can trace a docked workbook through its whole state machine — created → active → suspended → frozen → archived — and sees why 'freeze' is just 'stop the process, keep the SQLite file', no VM snapshot needed.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/lifecycle.ex (the @transitions map, idle auto-demotion policy: 15 min → suspend, 24 h → freeze; clone_for/3 template-clone-per-tenant; freeze = copy the VFS file to cold storage; litestream replication noted); runtime/host/control_plane.ex (the SQLite session registry — instances table with id/tenant/state/vfs_path; 'SQLite is the control plane, the data plane is each Instance's VFS'); runtime/host/instance/supervisor.ex.

subs.title: alive while closed
subs.dek: The reader learns how a workbook keeps working with nobody watching: keeper workers ticking agent defs on intervals, singleton vs crew scheduling, lifecycle specs that decide what each tick is, and schedules declared in the org source.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/keeper.ex (env contract: WB_KEEPER_DEF / WB_KEEPER_INTERVAL_MS / plan-vs-edit modes; singleton facade over keeper/worker.ex; keeper/crew.ex one-worker-per-agent); runtime/host/keeper/lifecycle.ex (optional state-machine spec consulted per tick); runtime/host/workflow.ex (workflows parsed from org with their schedules surfaced); the live proof is the lander fleet (examples/living-lander) whose commits ARE the public changelog via the keeper's tenant repo.

subs.title: the two planes
subs.dek: The reader understands why one Nexus runs two separate HTTP surfaces — an authed control plane and an anonymous GET-only content plane — and how a single BEAM node serves many custom domains via an ETS-backed SNI registry, no reverse proxy.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/public_web.ex (hard isolation rules: no Auth plug, GET-only, no Dock/commands/secrets routes exist; the 'served by workbooks' marker; /_changes and /_activity feeds); runtime/host/web.ex (the authed control plane, WB_WEB=1); runtime/host/application.ex web/0 (control on PORT 4000, public on PUBLIC_PORT 4001 + PUBLIC_TLS_PORT 4443 with sni_fun); runtime/host/domains.ex (host→app registry; unknown SNI host gets no cert so the handshake can't complete — admission gate). Deployed shape: public plane exposed, control plane internal+locked (lander-live).

subs.title: tenants behind one door
subs.dek: The reader sees how multi-tenancy is enforced rather than promised: the single/multi posture switch, the five-rung auth ladder, why a spoofable x-tenant header is rejected the moment isolation matters, and how every broker scopes to the tenant.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/tenancy.ex (WB_TENANCY_MODE single|multi — 'the one place the mode is read'); runtime/host/auth.ex (the auth ladder: public allowlist → desktop token → WB_PUBLIC_BEARER lock → BetterAuth/Guardian JWT where the org IS the tenant → dev x-tenant fallback only when unlocked AND single-tenant); runtime/host/lifecycle.ex clone_for/3 (per-tenant VFS copies from a read-only blueprint); runtime/host/secret_broker.ex + revocation.ex (per-tenant secret scoping and revocation); deploy/config.ex validate rejects multi-tenant-on-sqlite.

subs.title: one file, two places
subs.dek: The reader stands up a Nexus both ways — a cloud-identical krunvm microVM on their laptop and a Fly deploy — and understands deployment.org as inert declarative config where moving to the cloud is editing one property.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/deploy/config.ex (deployment.org parsed as a hand-rolled :PROPERTIES: scan, never executed; validate/1 encodes the honest combos — s3 needs bucket+endpoint, postgres/s3 secrets live in env never the file); runtime/host/deploy/machine.ex (local place = krunvm microVM: case-sensitive APFS volume preflight, create/start/delete contract, discovery file); runtime/host/deploy/backend.ex (provider seam: adding a cloud = drop a directory with bootstrap.sh filling five hooks); cli/deploy-kit/deployments/local.org + cloud-saas.org and cli/deploy-kit/providers/fly/bootstrap.sh (the shipped examples). Backs the parent's 'dev is prod' section with the actual verbs: init / validate / apply / status.

subs.title: the descriptor
subs.dek: How a handful of manifest keywords — #+EXEC, #+BUILD_SRC, #+BUILD_LANG, #+CAPS, #+CLI_BIN, #+TRUST — turn a folder of plain text into a buildable, runnable, capability-scoped toolkit with zero per-toolkit glue.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/toolkits.ex (parse_descriptor/1, the P4 build-descriptor section, the tagged BUILD_SRC forms crate:/git:/path:/wasm:/gobuild:/zigbuild:, runtimes/*.org multi-entry sets, build_text/3); toolkits/AUTHORING.org (the operational authoring standard); real manifests across toolkits/* (e.g. toolkits/glyphs, toolkits/ffmpeg); toolkits/toolkit-forge/skills/write-manifest.org

subs.title: the import ramp
subs.dek: Anything → toolkit: how wbx toolkit import sniffs nine source shapes (Claude skills, MCP configs, OpenAPI specs, npm/pip CLIs, cursor rules, AGENTS.md…), mechanically translates docs to org, and scaffolds a real manifest + skill tree — with carried scripts honestly flagged as untrusted.
subs.evidence: cli/src/import.rs (Kind enum with 9 detected shapes, detect() shape-sniffing, md_to_org() the 'honest 90%' translator, write_scaffold(), per-kind parsers incl. import_mcp_server synthesizing launch scripts so the audit can judge them, import_openapi making a skill per operation); stage 2 auto-runs via crate::audit::audit_static at the end of import()

subs.title: the wasm audit
subs.dek: Ready, convertible, or blocked: how the static dependency audit classifies every carried script against the wasm lanes, writes findings INTO the toolkit's own manifest, and emits a checkbox fix-up plan an agent can work through to done — with --fix closing the loop as push → build → verify.
subs.evidence: cli/src/audit.rs (Class::{Ready,Convertible,Blocked}, classify_interpreter/classify_binary truth tables — jq ready, curl→Dock, python blocked, docker blocked; worst-of roll-up; write_into_manifest 'the artifact carries its own audit'; fixup_plan() generating ** TODO [0/n] with per-finding recipe() steps; audit() --fix running toolkit_push/build/verify)

subs.title: the compiler lanes
subs.dek: The crux bet of the toolkit layer: C, Rust, Zig, Go, and JS compilers that are themselves compiled to WebAssembly, so untrusted source is built entirely inside the sandbox — c4, mrustc-to-C, zig1's C backend, yaegi interpretation, and QuickJS embedding, each a different trick to dodge native execution.
subs.evidence: runtime/compilers/README.org (zero-native-execution thesis); per-lane manifests: c/manifest.org (c4, compile-and-run), rust/manifest.org (mrustc → C → clang lane, e2e proof), zig/manifest.org (zig1.wasm stage1, compile-to-c), go/manifest.org (yaegi interpret-in-sandbox, wbgosrc custom section), js/manifest.org (QuickJS-ng + harness.c); rust/CRATES-COVERAGE.org + PROC-MACROS-PLAN.org for the honest frontier

subs.title: shimming node
subs.dek: How npm packages cross into the sandbox without npm install ever running: resolve and bundle at build time, then satisfy require('fs') and friends with host-brokered shims so Node-shaped code runs on QuickJS inside wasm.
subs.evidence: runtime/compilers/js/bundle/bundlejob.js (the build-time bundler), runtime/compilers/js/shims/*.js (fs, http/https, crypto, buffer, process, path… the Node-surface shims), js/harness_dock.c + harness.c (the Javy.IO/console contract and Dock bridge); audit.rs's npm findings point here ('resolve + bundle at toolkit build time'); memory: wb-spy/wb-e1x epics complete

subs.title: the promotion ladder
subs.dek: Session → workspace → registry: an agent writes a source file, build-inline registers it as a command in one step, and promote materializes it as a real source-owned toolkit — org owns the spec, wasm owns the artifact, and self-authoring never widens granted capabilities.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/toolkits.ex (build_inline_text/3 'no manifest ceremony' write→build→content-address→register; promote_text/4 with reserved-name and language guards; lang_layout/2 per-language source layouts; promote_manifest/promote_skill generating the scaffold; the Library.store/Library.install registry rung named in the promote docstring); parent lesson's #compose section only gestures at this with 'one command'

subs.title: signing and trust
subs.dek: What the signature actually binds: an Ed25519 did:key signature over the canonical manifest body ties the declared contract (EXEC/CAPS/BUILD_SRC) to an author identity, the build gate refuses any unsigned or tampered third-party toolkit, and the sandbox bounds damage regardless — two layers, distinct jobs.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/toolkits.ex (sign_text/3 strip-then-sign canonicalization, manifest_provenance/1 verification, trust_checks/2, the supply-chain gate in build_text/3: 'REFUSED — third-party toolkit with invalid provenance'; #+TRUST first-party vs third-party, first-party location-trust rationale in the threat-model comment); Workbooks.Git.did/sign/verify_sig as the shared crypto

subs.title: proving a toolkit
subs.dek: Verify and eval as the toolkit's quality gates: structural checks (manifest, skills, exec, caps, provenance), then bundled evals/*.org cases where an agent is run against a :TASK: with the toolkit's own manual injected and a judge model scores the result and tool trace against a :RUBRIC:.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/toolkits.ex (verify_text/2 structural + exec_checks + cap_checks + trust_checks; eval_text/2 and run_eval_case — Tier 2 agent_judge_case with :TASK:/:RUBRIC:/:MAX_STEPS:, judge/4 PASS-FAIL scoring; honest disabling of native :role eval per wb-9ja); toolkits/EVALS.org (the eval-case format); toolkits/toolkit-forge/skills/verify-toolkit.org

subs.title: reading org
subs.dek: Learn the whole grammar in one sitting — headlines, tags, TODO states, drawers, timestamps, source blocks — by drilling each construct against the kernel's actual parse output, with side-by-side markdown comparisons showing exactly what structure markdown throws away.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs parse_headlines returns JSON rows (level/title/state/tags/props/scheduled/deadline) — perfect for paste-org-see-JSON drills; runtime/kernel/src/browser_abi.rs + Cargo.toml `browser` feature exist explicitly 'for the learn-site notebooks' (oql_parse_headlines/oql_render exported to wasm32-unknown-unknown), so the drills can run live in-page; the parent's own easter egg (web/learn/org.html lines 30-41) is a valid org comment to dissect; web/learn/org.html#why-not covers the markdown argument at concept level only — this goes hands-on.

subs.title: properties drawers
subs.dek: How :PROPERTIES: drawers turn a headline into a typed record — the key-value mechanism behind toolkit manifests, agent identities, and the spec block inside every learn page.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs headline_of() reads hl.properties() and uppercases keys into a BTreeMap; runtime/toolkits/huniq/manifest.org (:ID:/:CLI_BIN:/:STATUS:/:SKILL_DIR:) and runtime/examples/agents/analyst.org (:MODEL:/:TOOLKITS:/:TYPE: — an agent's whole identity is a drawer); schedule_of() reads the :SCHEDULE: prop for cron; even web/learn/org.html's own <script id="workbook-spec"> is a properties drawer driving the page.

subs.title: timestamps and repeaters
subs.dek: The full date grammar — active <…> vs inactive […], SCHEDULED vs DEADLINE, +1d/.+/++ repeaters, and the :SCHEDULE: cron escape hatch — and how a timestamp on a headline becomes a workflow that actually runs every morning.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs parse_timestamp() implements the exact grammar (angle/square brackets, time tokens, three repeater prefixes) and Timestamp::json() emits {at, repeat, active}; schedule_of() prefers :SCHEDULE: cron over SCHEDULED; runtime/examples/wb/nightly-digest.org carries `SCHEDULED: <2026-06-06 Sat 06:00 +1d>` on a :workflow: headline; runtime/host/workflow.ex surfaces the schedule in every run record.

subs.title: tangling
subs.dek: Literate programming, weaponized: how source blocks plus six header args (:deps :uses :in :out :persist :dir) compile a document into a WIT-world-shaped build plan — components, capability imports, and a DAG of :out→:in edges.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs tangle_plan/build_world/parse_args (the six header args, including Motoko-style :persist and :dir for real project dirs); sig_of() derives imports/exports/edges from header args alone; cli/src/kernel.rs `wb tangle` runs it locally with no runtime; cli/SPEC.md lists tangle as a kernel-local verb; runtime/examples/wb/nightly-digest.org is a three-language tangled workflow.

subs.title: your first workflow
subs.dek: Write a multi-language workflow from a blank file — headline by headline, component by component — then tangle it, lint it, fix the diagnostics, and run the DAG.
subs.evidence: runtime/examples/wb/nightly-digest.org (rust→js→go, :uses workbook:vfs/query, llm/complete, net/email) is the template; cli/src/kernel.rs gives the loop verbs (`wb query` / `wb tangle` / `wb lint`); runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs validate() produces the teachable failure modes (component with no source block, input with no upstream producer); runtime/host/workflow.ex executes the plan topologically, piping along edges.

subs.title: the kernel
subs.dek: Inside OQL — one 550-line pure Rust crate (parse, tangle, validate, render on orgize) that ships as three surfaces from the same source: a native rlib in the wb CLI, a WIT-typed wasm Component in the runtime and desktop, and a raw ptr/len build running in this very website.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs (pure string→string API, no host calls, no unsafe in the component path); runtime/kernel/wit/world.wit (the workbooks:oql world — six exports); runtime/kernel/src/browser_abi.rs (packed-u64 ABI for in-browser instantiation); runtime/kernel/Cargo.toml documents the cdylib+rlib split; consumers: cli/src/kernel.rs (native), runtime/host/oql.ex (wasm component), runtime/host/publish.ex + public_web.ex (render to HTML).

subs.title: the upgrade gate
subs.dek: Why you can diff two versions of a document and refuse a breaking deploy — check_upgrade applies WIT/Candid-style subtyping to org workflows: exports may grow but never shrink, imports may shrink but never grow, output types are frozen.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs check_upgrade() + world_sigs() implement the full gate (workflow removed = error, export removed = error, new capability required = warn, component output type changed = error); the Motoko-lineage comments are in-source; exposed as check-upgrade in runtime/kernel/wit/world.wit and via runtime/host/oql.ex — the proof that org being parseable means deploys can be safe, the parent page's 'testable by machines' claim made concrete.

subs.title: the loop
subs.dek: What a single agent run actually is — the model→tools→append cycle, why every tool call is wall-clock bounded, and how a run leaves a fully readable trace.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/agent.ex — loop/2 (LLM → tool_calls → exec → append → loop), exec_bounded/2 (150s per-tool kill), max_steps bound, done tool, events.org org-mode log + always-on _steps.jsonl telemetry; tool surface (shell/search/fetch/web_search/vfs_*) and the exec trust split (@exec_tools git/publish/image, host-brokered, no native exec — wb-9ja).

subs.title: authoring an agent
subs.dek: Write a complete agent definition in plain org — the :agent: node, the system-prompt heading, declared toolkits — and understand exactly how the runtime parses and runs it.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/agent_def.ex — parse of the :agent: node (:ID:/:MODEL:/:TOOLKITS:/:TAGLINE:), the `** System prompt` heading rule (and the empty-prompt failure it guards against), toolkit auto-injection via Workbooks.Toolkits.injection_text; worked example: examples/living-lander/agent/agent.org (Waldo — mandate, ground rules, cadence, tooling, orientation budget).

subs.title: the context repo
subs.dek: An agent's memory is a workbook — a git repo of plain files it reads, writes, and commits — not a vector store bolted on the side; the board, the canon, and the logs all live in one place anyone can diff.
subs.evidence: examples/living-lander/agent/ — plan.org board protocol (TODO/NEXT/DOING/DONE states), context.org, design.org, design-gate.org, sections.org, skills/, rem/; runtime/host/agent.ex `search` tool ('no separate memory store; the files ARE the memory'); runtime/host/keeper.ex ('the keeper's commits ARE the public changelog', WB_TENANT repo as workdir).

subs.title: spawning
subs.dek: How a run comes to exist and stays alive — supervised sessions you start with one call, then poll or stream while the agent works for minutes, surviving the caller that launched it.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/agent_session.ex — DynamicSupervisor + Registry session start, the spawned run process, on_step fan-out to WS subscribers, GET /api/run/:id poll + /stream, WB_RUN env so a run can address itself; runtime/host/keeper/crew.ex worker_spec (one supervised Worker per crew member, staggered starts).

subs.title: orchestration
subs.dek: How standing agents keep a cadence — the keeper's tick, a lifecycle state machine declared in org, and a crew of workers sharing one board with claims as protocol, not locks.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/keeper.ex (singleton facade, tick engine), runtime/host/keeper/worker.ex (instantiable core, crash-safety, NO-WORK fast-forward, catch-up scheduling), runtime/host/keeper/lifecycle.ex (org-declared state machine: :KIND:/:REPEAT:/:NEXT:/:MIN-INTERVAL:, position survives restarts), runtime/host/keeper/crew.ex (crew manifest, stagger, Crew.Gate concurrency cap, board claims as def-level protocol).

subs.title: configuring at runtime
subs.dek: Every knob that shapes an agent without touching engine code — the env contract, org manifests, model and toolkit props, intervals, and the exec trust grant.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/keeper.ex env contract (WB_KEEPER_DEF/INTERVAL_MS/MODE/CONTINUOUS, WB_TENANT, WB_LIFECYCLE_DEF), runtime/host/keeper/crew.ex (WB_CREW_DEF manifest + WB_CREW_STAGGER_MS/MAX_CONCURRENT, per-agent :DEF:/:LIFECYCLE:/:INTERVAL:), runtime/host/dreams.ex (WB_DREAM_MODEL, WB_DREAM_MIN_INTERVAL_MS), agent_def.ex :MODEL:/:TOOLKITS: props and run-time opts (max_steps, exec, model override).

subs.title: human in the loop
subs.dek: Insert a real human checkpoint into a live run — a review canvas the agent opens, a commit the human makes, and a FIFO the agent polls mid-loop to pick the verdict up.
subs.evidence: toolkits/ctk/manifest.org (CTK — 'a human-in-the-loop canvas', render EXEC shape) + skills/agent-review-loop.org, commit-connector.org, runtime-driving.org; runtime/host/agent_session.ex put_review/take_review (FIFO reviews, append-only review_log, durable per-run JSONL, live push to subscribers), WB_RUN + `wb ctk await $WB_RUN`.

subs.title: dreaming
subs.dek: What an agent does between runs — a sleep phase that digests telemetry, commits, and the backlog into a dream journal whose verdicts mechanically steer the next waking run.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/dreams.ex (REM epic wb-2ku: gather → dream model → fixed headings tale/goals/blue sky/fears/verdicts/carry; daydreams as ephemeral ≤40-word musings, audit-gated full dreams); examples/living-lander/agent/agent.org board protocol step 1 (apply newest dream's * verdicts: pick up → NEXT, put down → TODO) and orientation step 0 (* carry as resume state); examples/living-lander/agent/rem/.

subs.title: the mode model
subs.dek: How one binary serves two audiences — TTY detection, the --agent/--json switches, the {ok, verb, data, error} envelope, and the stable exit-code map an agent can branch on without parsing prose.
subs.evidence: cli/src/mode.rs (detect(), classify() heuristic→exit codes 3/4/5/6/7, render_ok/render_err, verb_path(), pick() gated to human mode, next_hint() verb chaining); contract tests in cli/tests/mode.rs (envelope on success, code 4 on not-found, piped default = plain text); spec in cli/SPEC.md § 'Ergonomics: two audiences, one binary'. Parent lesson shows the envelope; this goes inside how it's built and tested.

subs.title: org on stdin
subs.dek: Build real pipelines with the kernel verbs — query, tangle, and lint accept '-' for stdin, emit JSON, and compose with --json and jq so generated org never touches a temp file.
subs.evidence: cli/src/kernel.rs (read_org handles file == "-", oql::parse_headlines / tangle_plan / validate all return JSON); the embedded kernel is the same runtime/kernel crate the engine uses; cli/SPEC.md P3 'stdin pipelines across author/trust verbs' names the frontier; parent lesson § agents shows two one-liners but never teaches composition.

subs.title: doctor, status, completions
subs.dek: Wire wbx into your shell and let it check itself — doctor's report-not-judge contract (always exit 0, JSON for agents), the bare-wbx where-am-I landing, clap-generated completions, and upgrade's npm-aware self-update.
subs.evidence: cli/src/commands.rs:207 (doctor — 'reported not judged', exit 0); cli/src/main.rs (Doctor/Status/Open/Upgrade/Completions verbs, bare wbx routes through doctor at main.rs:258, completions via clap_complete); cli/src/local.rs upgrade(); spec rationale in cli/SPEC.md § 'The prime DX directive'.

subs.title: the intake ramp
subs.dek: A full walkthrough of wbx toolkit import — nine source kinds detected by shape, the wasm-lane audit that classifies every script ready/convertible/blocked, and the fix-up plan written as org TODOs an agent can execute.
subs.evidence: cli/src/import.rs (Kind enum: claude-skill/markdown/folder/mcp-server/openapi/npm-cli/pip-cli/cursor-rules/agents-md; detect() by shape, --as override); cli/src/audit.rs (Class Ready/Convertible/Blocked, classify_interpreter — sh/js ready, python blocked, classify_binary — curl→engine-brokered HTTP; findings written into manifest.org); taxonomy table in cli/SPEC.md § 'Import: anything → toolkit'. Parent covers the three stages in prose; this walks the actual detection and classification rules.

subs.title: declare, then converge
subs.dek: Stand up an engine with the deploy-kit — scaffold deployment.org with init, validate, apply, and watch one verb set converge a local container or a cloud provider, with secrets declared by name and never written into the artifact.
subs.evidence: cli/src/deploy/mod.rs (DeployVerb init/validate/apply/status/logs/down/local/doctor/secrets; provider-agnostic recipes — local container seam built in, anything else a providers/<place>/bootstrap.sh recipe, fly bundled via include_str!; secrets stored 0600 under the app dir, names in #+DEPLOY_SECRETS, values never in deployment.org); recipe spine at cli/deploy-kit/providers/_recipe.sh; cli/deploy-kit/deployments/*.org templates.

subs.title: inside the bundle
subs.dek: What wbx bundle actually writes — the wbundle/1 zip (workbook.html + workbook.org + vfs.sqlite + manifest.json), the lint gate that refuses to assemble a dirty source, and the Ed25519 did:key signature that makes verify mean something.
subs.evidence: cli/src/local.rs (bundle() — oql::render, diagnostics gate 'source has diagnostics — fix them first', sibling vfs.sqlite travels, manifest format 'wbundle/1', source ships in the artifact so recipients can unbundle + re-author; sign/verify — Ed25519 over canonical JSON, byte-compatible with the runtime's Workbooks.Manifest); parent lesson only says 'org + data + wasm → one artifact'.

subs.title: the capability seam
subs.dek: Why the same crate compiles to your laptop and into the engine's sandbox — one Io trait (http/read/write/spawn) as the only place the two targets differ, native std/reqwest on one side, Dock-brokered host imports on the other, plus engine discovery via runtime.json.
subs.evidence: cli/src/io.rs (trait Io, platform() compile-time impl pick, native module with Disco discovery mirroring Workbooks.Desktop.discovery_path — WB_DESKTOP_DIR / sh.workbooks/disco/runtime.json); cli/SPEC.md § 'The discipline that makes both targets work'; cli/src/dev.rs shows the seam's consequence (dev bails on wasm, agents use bundle); parent lesson § everywhere states the claim — this is the implementation.

subs.title: the implicit interpreter
subs.dek: How a plain TODO outline — no custom tags, nothing to learn — runs as a state machine: nesting decides composite vs leaf, :ORDERED: decides pipeline vs parallel, DONE tasks are skipped so every run is resumable.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/workflow/todo.ex (the whole interpreter: keywords, parse, run_set sequential/parallel, composite DONE/PARTIAL rollup, scratch/ working memory, retrieve blocks); runtime/host/web.ex POST /api/workflow/todo (async run + _status.json polling). The parent's #ready/#rounds sections describe the loop abstractly; this is the actual machine.

subs.title: validations
subs.dek: DONE is a claim until a check proves it — the three-rung ladder of plan validation (dangling inputs, missing langs), task acceptance (:done-when: and :check blocks run fail-closed in the WASM shell), and build conformance, which together turn drift from a shrug into a named diagnostic.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs validate() (dangling :in, component without source block); runtime/host/workflow/todo.ex validate/sh_ok ('unit tests for org mode', fail-closed via Workbooks.Shell, never native sh); runtime/host/conformance.ex (engine-world conformance at wb build); runtime/host/demos/kernel.ex demo_validate. Parent's #honest section promises 'drift detectable, with a name and a line number' — this lesson is that promise, mechanized. User-named topic.

subs.title: boards as renderings
subs.dek: Why there is no board model anywhere in the runtime — a board is the kernel's render() over the plan file plus a write path back into it, and any surface (kanban, status page, an agent's ready list) is the same one-file two-way binding.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs render() + wit/world.wit (render export); runtime/host/web.ex workbook_page (rendered org + ws/call write path back to the same runtime) and /api/workflow?plan=1 (the plan view with no execution); runtime/host/workflow.ex moduledoc: 'there is no separate board... no DSL, no board model'; _status.json per-task states as a live board in web.ex. Goes deeper than the parent's #boards section by showing the actual render/write seam.

subs.title: schedules
subs.dek: The full grammar of time in a plan — active vs inactive timestamps, +1w/.+/++ repeaters, the :SCHEDULE: cron property — and the keeper, the engine that actually fires them: workers, crews, lifecycle specs, and the breather between ticks.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs parse_timestamp (active/inactive, repeat tokens) + schedule_of (SCHEDULE cron prop wins over SCHEDULED timestamp); runtime/host/keeper.ex (singleton facade, env contract, tick intervals, continuous mode) + runtime/host/keeper/{worker,crew,lifecycle}.ex; runtime/host/workflow.ex surfaces schedule in every run record. Parent's #schedules section says 'the engine fires these' in one sentence — this is the engine. User-suggested topic.

subs.title: plan to world
subs.dek: What tangle_plan actually computes — edges inferred by matching :out to :in, exports as the outputs nobody consumed, imports from :uses, nested workflows as sub-worlds — and why the result is shaped like a WIT world on purpose.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs build_world/build_plan/sig_of/parse_args (:deps/:uses/:in/:out/:persist/:dir header args); runtime/kernel/wit/world.wit (the kernel itself rides the same Component Model it imposes); runtime/host/demos/kernel.ex demo_tangle/demo_nested/demo_persist. The parent's #compile section shows one diagram of this; the deep dive walks the actual inference, including :persist orthogonal persistence and :dir project references it never mentions. User-suggested topic (compile-to-world / components and edges).

subs.title: waves
subs.dek: How a compiled world executes — topological waves where every step whose predecessors are done runs in parallel, producers' stdout piped into consumers' stdin along the edges, and agent-lang components fanning out sub-agents inside the same DAG.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/package_manager.ex run_world/waves (wave computation, Task.async_stream max_concurrency 8, edge piping) and run_component_step (build + run as WASM filter); runtime/host/workflow.ex step/2 (agent-lang component = agent loop, source block as system prompt); runtime/host/web.ex POST /api/workflow. The parent shows three sequential 'rounds'; this shows why independent work actually runs at once.

subs.title: the upgrade gate
subs.dek: How a live plan changes safely — the Motoko/Candid-style subtyping rules (exports may grow but never shrink, imports may shrink but never grow, an output type may never change) that let the kernel refuse a breaking redeploy before it runs.
subs.evidence: runtime/kernel/src/lib.rs check_upgrade + world_sigs (the exact rules, error vs warn diagnostics); runtime/kernel/wit/world.wit check-upgrade export; runtime/host/demos/kernel.ex demo upgrade; pairs with :persist in parse_args (state that survives the redeploy the gate just approved). Wholly absent from the parent — pure new depth.

subs.title: the run record
subs.dek: What a run leaves behind and why it splits in two — org files in scratch/ for the agent's thinking, SQLite _telemetry.db for the queryable task log — and how the ledger seals _steps.jsonl into a hash-chained, Ed25519-signed, git-anchored record nobody can quietly rewrite.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/workflow/telemetry.ex (the scratch/SQLite split, task_events schema, single-writer design); runtime/host/ledger.ex (hash-chain over raw log bytes, did:key signature, git anchor, verify/1); runtime/host/workflow/todo.ex run/2 calls both at run-end. Answers the parent's 'when did this last run, and what happened?' line with the actual artifacts.

subs.title: volumes
subs.dek: The disk isn't one undifferentiated tree — it's three named regions (workspace, memory, tmp) with different lifetimes, and knowing which one a byte lives in tells you whether it persists, travels, or evaporates.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/vfs.ex (@volumes ~w(workspace memory tmp), the (volume, path) primary key, clear/2); runtime/host/lifecycle.ex (resume/3 clears tmp, workspace+memory persist across freeze/resume); runtime/host/private.ex (@public_volumes — only workspace ships)

subs.title: sql over the disk
subs.dek: How to actually query the disk: the vfs table's real schema, the Policy-gated vfs-query Dock import your component calls, error-as-JSON safety so a bad query can never crash the engine, and one SQL statement run across a whole library of workbooks.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/vfs.ex (CREATE TABLE vfs (volume, path, content, mtime), query_json/2 returns JSON rows or a JSON error — never a host crash); runtime/host/instance/imports.ex (the "vfs" cap grants the vfs-query import; gating is by construction); runtime/host/library.ex (Library.query/2 — cross-workbook query-through over every member's vfs.sqlite)

subs.title: the docked disk
subs.dek: What 'the disk gets a heartbeat' actually means: the instance lifecycle state machine, freeze/resume as a file copy instead of a VM snapshot, WAL-mode streaming to off-box replicas, and clone-per-tenant so a thousand users each get their own copy of one template disk.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/lifecycle.ex (created→active→suspended→frozen→archived transitions, idle auto-demotion thresholds, freeze/resume/clone_for); runtime/host/litestream.ex (enable_wal, replicate to file:// or s3://R2, one-shot restore); parent lesson's #readings section only gestures at this

subs.title: what ships, what stays
subs.dek: Sharing exposes the work, never the session that produced it — one boundary module decides what leaves on every egress path (bundle, git, library), so agent memory, scratch files, and telemetry stay home unless the owner explicitly opts in.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/private.ex (the single public/private source of truth: private globs, gitignore_lines, public_volumes); runtime/host/vfs.ex (public_only/1 deletes private volumes + VACUUMs before egress); runtime/host/bundle.ex (ship/4 strips by default, include_private: true is the explicit opt-in, manifest records private_included)

subs.title: unbundling
subs.dek: Getting everything back out: the .wbundle is a plain zip any tool can open — workbook.html, vfs.sqlite, the org source, a manifest — and one CLI verb unpacks the whole disk to ordinary files on your real disk, zip-slip-guarded, with re-authoring possible because the source travels.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/bundle.ex (pack/unpack/ship/restore, format wbundle/1 — 'a plain zip, any tool can open it'); cli/src/local.rs (wb bundle / wb unbundle local verbs, unzip_bytes_to with unsafe-path refusal, workbook.org included so 'recipients can unbundle + re-author')

subs.title: sealed sections
subs.dek: How part of a shipped disk can be ciphertext to everyone and plaintext to the right person: AES-256-GCM envelopes whose content keys never ride in the bundle — they're escrowed at the runtime, released only after a posture check, and optionally wrapped to a recipient's DID so there's no plaintext-key honeypot anywhere.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/bundle/sealed.ex (wbseal1 envelope, AAD-bound key_id so entries can't be relabelled, fail-closed open); runtime/host/bundle/escrow.ex (runtime-held keys, release via POST /rcp/key/:key_id only after Workbooks.Access.enforce); runtime/host/bundle/key_wrap.ex (X25519 sealed-box wrapping to a recipient identity); runtime/host/access.ex

subs.title: foreign tables
subs.dek: Make FROM reach past the file: register a data-source plugin and a query against its entity routes to a live API instead of the local store — or run the sync daemon and keep a resident, queryable, agent-airgapped mirror of the outside world inside the disk.
subs.evidence: runtime/host/data_source.ex (the data-source behaviour + entity registry); runtime/host/federation.ex (discover plugins from manifest.org, route SELECT … FROM <entity> to the plugin, else fall through to the local VFS); runtime/host/plugin/sync.ex (interval pull mirroring rows into :task: org nodes in the VFS); runtime/host/data_source/http.ex (the generic HTTP reference source)
